utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone as well in this courtroom and for those assisting us just outside the courtroom. I did understand that in order to proceed, that there is a possibility that we would sit a bit longer today. That would mean that we'll, if this is also okay as far as Sarajevo is concerned, that we would have a bit longer second break, not 20 minutes, but half an hour, and then continue a bit longer. I understood that all those assisting us have been consulted on these plans. Let me then just check on whether the link with Sarajevo is running. I see on some screens, not on mine at this very moment -- yes, I have it on my screen now as well -- that the representative of the registry in Sarajevo is present. I think, Mr. Ierace, we could continue the examination-in-chief of the witness after the witness has been brought in but not until after having heard what Mr. Piletta-Zanin wants to bring to my attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, Your Honours, good morning. Thank you for giving me the floor. It is simply this: Yesterday, we asked a question of the Prosecution which is of fundamental importance for the Defence, and the question was, how is it possible that a text which in Serbian, in its Serbian original, does not include certain line of text, certain words, how can it be translated into another language, into a text with some lines which we know do not exist in the source document? That question will -- could arise whenever we have a medical document which is submitted by the Prosecution, and I think that the question of methodology is very important. I would like to invite the Prosecution to tell us how is that possible, because apparently other documents which were submitted to -- the other documents were submitted to -- for translation which the Defence or anyone else has never seen. And to our mind, this is really a fundamental issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the Prosecution would like to respond on it, we do not oppose against it. But we'll not give an order to respond to the question, at least not at this very moment. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would prefer not to respond to it at this stage, and continue with the evidence if that's acceptable to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's acceptable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, Mr. Ierace, if at some later stage you would be able, whether in writing or just in a short oral statement, to give us an explanation, if you can give it, that would, of course, be of assistance for the Chamber in order to better understand how the preparation of the Prosecution's case was organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will do that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. One question, then: In that case, and under those conditions, since we do not have now the response of the Prosecution, the Defence clearly says that it will be, therefore, handicapped in its cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand your position, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Mr. Ierace, I'll now ask the Registry in Sarajevo to escort the witness into the courtroom. Ms. Philpott, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom -- in the videoroom, I would say. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, just a moment. Sometimes we have problem with the transcript. I'm re-reading the English transcript. What I said, that "these witnesses" and not "this witness." Let us make it very precise. I mean, this will prejudice our cross-examination for all -- prejudice our cross-examination of all the witnesses with whom we may have this kind of problem. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your clarification, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kapetanovic. Can you hear me --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Good morning. I can 1 1 hear you very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Kapetanovic, may I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony. Now your examination by counsel for the -- by counsel for the Prosecution will continue. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Ierace: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday afternoon, you said that, as we saw on the video, you indicated precisely where you were at the time that you and the other two men were shot. You also agreed that --

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also told us that the photograph in which you can look in all directions was --

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You told us that that photograph showed the view from where you were shot. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the assistance of Ms. Philpott, can you see on your computer screen now the view from where you were shot of the tall white building with the blue band?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at that photograph, do you agree that the white building with the blue band is on the opposite corner to where you were shot?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the assistance of Ms. Philpott, would you look again this morning at the photograph on which you placed your signature and some black lines, that is, Exhibit P3265.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We are sorry. Could the witness please repeat his answer. There is pretty bad interference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, we were unable to hear clearly your last answer. Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the photograph in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you said that the student hostel, which appears on the right of that photograph, was damaged, and it was possible to see through the building because of the damage. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you walked along Ante Babica Street on that day, was it possible to see through the floors of that building?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't because it was too high up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, yesterday you told us that you believed that the shot or shots were fired from the school for the blind, or I think you might have called it the home for the blind. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. As far as I could see, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever been to the home for the blind?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never entered the building, but I frequently pass by. I know the area very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many buildings made up the home for the blind, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has the ground floor and two floors above it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean it was one building or more than one building?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The blind people's home is one building, but next to it was an old people's home, but it is a little bit further away from the blind people's home, about 50 -- about a hundred metres away. So I cannot be quite sure, but I think that the bullets which hit us came from the blind people's home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look again at the photograph taken from above, which for the transcript is P3279OA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, could you ask this photograph to be put on the ELMO in Sarajevo. I was informed that there might be some confusion now and then which -- to what is exactly in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. All right. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that photograph, can you see the school for the blind?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a bit further away, I can see it. But between this small building and the students hostel, that is where you can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please point to the school for the blind on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness points to the top left-hand corner of photograph P3279OA, and in particular there is a road in the top left-hand corner. The witness points to a building with a white roof on the right side of the road. Mr. President, I understand there may be a spare copy of P3279OA in Sarajevo. Perhaps Ms. Philpott could confirm that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] I have one colour photograph, P3279OA, and I have a black and white photocopy of the same photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I propose to ask the witness to circle the building that he just indicated. I assume that the photograph, that is, the colour photograph, before the witness is not the original of the exhibit that was tendered before Mr. Dziho.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just confirm with the registry here in The Hague whether the originally tendered colour copy is here in The Hague. Yes, it is confirmed to me that the original photograph, coloured photograph, is in The Hague. So even the coloured copy in Sarajevo must be a spare copy. Would you please put that on the ELMO, Ms. Philpott. It is on the ELMO, I think. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, would you please take a blue pen, that is, a pen with blue ink, and place a circle -- draw a circle around the building which you think is the school for the blind on that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think that would be P3279OB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, yesterday, you said a bullet hit your belt during this incident. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What part of your clothing --

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said was that it grazed my belt, just ever so slightly, and it hit those other two: Vucic, the one who died, and Franjic, who was hit in the stomach. So I wasn't really hit. It barely brushed against my belt. I didn't even feel it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, as the bullet grazed your belt, where was that part of the belt on your body? In other words, was the part that was grazed in the middle or to one side or behind you?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My left side, in the centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please stand up and point to the part of your waist where the bullet grazed your belt.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness indicates his left side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may sit down again, Mr. Kapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain to us why it is you think the bullet came from your right side if it grazed your belt on your left side?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assumption is that these two, that is Franjic was the first one and was hit in the stomach. The other one was hit in the kidney and he was severely injured. And the assumption is that perhaps there was yet another bullet, but it is just an assumption. I don't know. The sniper who hit him, perhaps when that happened, perhaps I was one step ahead or behind and that is how I was caught in the waist. But that is merely an assumption. I don't know. But that is how it happened anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recollect exactly which direction you were facing at the time of the shooting?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were facing Dobrinja. We were moving towards Dobrinja, so we were facing Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. But I wonder whether you remember with precision how your body was placed at the exact moment of the shooting.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It faces -- well, as we walked, it was to one side, that is, in the direction of Dobrinja as we walked, because we were walking abreast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. So I must confess I missed the actual marking, and I'd like to ask Ms. Philpott in Sarajevo perhaps if the coloured photograph, P3279OB, is still on the ELMO, just to zoom in so that I can... It is, yes. It's on your screen. And perhaps exactly show there where the witness marked the home for the blind. Could you please perhaps go a bit more to the left upper corner of the photograph where I would ... Yes. I see the marking now. Thank you very much. Ms. Pilipovic, is the Defence ready to cross-examine the witness? Mr. Kapetanovic, you will now be examined by counsel for the Defence. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kapetanovic, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that in 1994, you lived in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us which part of town you lived in?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Alipasino Polje Trg Solidarnosti, or Solidarity Square.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, since when have you lived in Alipasino Polje?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1992, May. We fled from the house we were in until that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you fled in May 1992 from the house, the facility, can you tell us where you had lived up until that time before you fled?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stupsko Brdo. Stup hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, how far Stupsko Brdo is from Alipasino Polje?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps 2 kilometres away, because Stupsko Brdo is a rather long stretch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In May 1992, at Alipasino Polje, did you flee together with the whole of your family? Did you all flee?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, which army, from 1992 when you fled, up until the period in August 1994, which army controlled Stupsko Brdo? The Defence is interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you which army.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're saying that Stupsko Brdo was controlled by the army of Yugoslavia. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know that Stupsko Brdo was also controlled by the army of the Croatian defence council and the army of BH? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not that part of Stupsko Brdo. They weren't in control of that part of Stupsko Brdo because they couldn't reach that area because the actual front was at Stupsko Brdo, towards the Oslobodenje building. If you know the Oslobodenje building, it is 12 metres in depth, which is where the army of Yugoslavia was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you reached Alipasino Polje and took up residence in the apartment on Solidarity Square, Trg Solidarnosti, can you tell us who was in the flat when you went there?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, could you please repeat your answer. The interpreters could not hear you.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was living in the apartment belonging to my son-in-law and daughter. And it was building number 13.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have said that in 1994, in the month of April, you were going out for a walk with your neighbour, Ivan Franjic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, correct. Not only Ivan Franjic, but Augustin Vucic, too. There were three of us, and he was the third.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us how often in the course of 1992, when you moved house, up until the moment when the incident took place, how often you would go out for a walk?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from time to time, one, two, three days, depending, because the front line was close by. So we didn't dare move around much, because you could target this area with infantry weapons, but we went out for walks nonetheless and that's why we got what we got.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us in that period of time, that is to say, during your walks, when you went out for a walk, did you always walk around the same area that you went out for a walk in on that critical day?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you went out for your walks during that period, can you tell us whether there was any firing in that part of town, any shooting?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't, not when we went out for walks. But on that particular day, there was, of course. It happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, or rather can you confirm, that on that particular day, as you said you went out for a walk at about 10.00. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I say to you that your friend, Ivan Franjic, gave a statement to the investigators of the Prosecution on the 21st of November, 1995, page 2 of the statement which your friend gave - it is Document 0090-6701 in the B/C/S version, that is - Part 6, I'm going to read out what your friend says here, or paragraph 6. "I can't remember at the moment what time it was exactly on that particular day when I was hit, but it was in the afternoon." Now, can you tell us what is correct? Is it true -- is the time that you say you went out for a walk correct, or was it indeed the afternoon as your friend says?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I claim that it was before noon at about 10.00. Perhaps the man couldn't remember when it was because he was rather seriously wounded. So maybe he was a little upset, too, because his wounds were very serious, so maybe he didn't remember. But I claim it was before noon at about 10.00. Now, whether it was a few minutes before or after 10.00, I can't say for sure, but I'm certain that it was about 10.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, can you tell us the following: The area you lived in, that is to say Trg Solidarnosti, and part of Alipasino Polje, which as you're moving towards Dobrinja there's a square there, do you happen to know within that particular area there were any military facilities belonging to the army of --

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, we didn't see anything, they didn't exist the way we walked. We didn't see any military facilities, nor were there any soldiers around. The only thing that I can say is that towards the Aleksa Santic School was where the army was, and the soldiers belonging to it. They had control over that area there. They had the area in their own hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether at Trg Solidarnosti, Solidarity Square, and the Zavnobih Square, which is the other square on Alipasino Polje --

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I know it well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether on these two squares, in these two squares, there were police stations in the two squares?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Solidarity Square, or 50 metres away from the square, there was a police station. I don't know about any other police station, whether there was another one or not. But I remember that particular one on Trg Solidarnosti.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I tell you that your friend Ivan Franjic in his statement dated the 21st of November, 1995, on page 2 of document 0090-6701, the B/C/S version, in paragraph 3, line 2, says the following: "The area I live in in Alipasino Polje is a residential settlement, and there was a kiosk there and a bakery and a butcher's shop. That's where the HVO was. The HVO was there and a police station." Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. But in continuation on Trg Solidarnosti, some 200 metres away, there was a little small thing. But the police did exist, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the HVO facility? What building was that located in? What kind of building was it housed in?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a ground floor -- of the ground floor and an office space, office premises. There was nothing else there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During 1992, 1993, and 1994, in that part of town, did you happen to see soldiers belonging to the HVO, HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever we went by there, I didn't see any. I didn't see them. It was a sort of warehouse, something like that there and I never saw any soldiers there. I, myself, I personally. Maybe somebody did, but I didn't personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992 and 1993 and 1994, in that area, did you see soldiers belonging to the BH army perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anyone. There were some individuals going to and fro, but not as a group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you saw them individually coming back from their shift, I think you said, can you tell us what they were wearing, those people that you saw?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were wearing normal clothes, the type that the army wore, the type that soldiers wore, the yellow, olive-green, grey, striped type of uniform clothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you happen to see these people with arms, with weapons?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, there was nobody with any weapons there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that part of town, the part of town you lived in and where the police station was, did you happen to see policemen, any policemen?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. But without any weapons, not armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what they were wearing? What kind of uniforms did they have?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the ordinary type of uniform that they used to wear before the war. You know the type of uniform that policemen wore, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that particular day when you went out for your walk, did all three of you meet up at the same time, or did you and Mr. Franjic start out on your walk earlier?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the two of us lived in one facility, one building, we went on to Ante Babica where we -- Street, where we met up with Augustin Vucic, and he went with us, and we walked in the direction of Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, in Branko Bujic Street when you went out for your walk, the place you said that the incident took place, can you tell us what number it was, what number of the building?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say. I don't know. I didn't look. I wasn't interested. It didn't occur to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you told us and confirmed that you know where the HVO headquarters was and the police station, could you -- do you also confirm that that was on Trg Solidarnosti where you lived?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I lived on Trg Solidarnosti in building number 13. It was Trg Solidarnosti. That's where we lived and moved around, because it was dangerous to move around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said yesterday that the front line, in relation to the place or rather the street you were walking along, was about three to four hundred metres away. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not 300 and 400. I said 200 metres, not more than 200 metres. We were walking around there, and the front line was -- or the trenches and communicating trenches were 200 metres away from where we were walking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that the part of town which you say you assume the shot came from when the three of you were walking was under the control of the army of Republika Srpska. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also confirm that the part of town you were walking along was under the control of the BH army? Is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that in the part of town called Alipasino Polje where you lived, yourself, that there was the BH army there, that it was located there?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could see them individually, but I couldn't see groups. I didn't see groups of them. Just individually, I would see a soldier here and there when they were coming and going. But that there was a headquarters or a group, I didn't see that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that on that particular day, you set off towards Dobrinja to go for a walk. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I went towards Dobrinja, but we didn't go right there. But at the turning point going into town following the tram, that's where we went to. We went as far as that. We didn't go further on. But we were facing the direction of Dobrinja, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were living in the apartment at that time, and when I say that time and period, I'm talking about 1992, between 1992 and 1994 when you took up residence there, did you happen to learn that in Dobrinja, the 5th Motorised Brigade had been set up there, had been stationed there?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that period of time, did you happen to learn that at Alipasino Polje, in the part you lived in, the headquarters of three battalions were located belonging to the 5th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that in that part of town, and I'm speaking of Alipasino Polje and the part of town called Nedzarici, whether during that period of time in that part of town there was any fighting?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that. I am aware of that because there was a lot of shooting. So that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you then confirm that there was fighting between the army of Republika Srpska and the BH army? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, that was what it was, but I wasn't with them so I can't say. But I do know that they were shooting at each other. Now who actually did the shooting, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please -- can you confirm that the part of the street called Alija Branko Bujic which you took to go for your walk, looking towards the students hostel that you identified and indicated on the photograph, was that part of town protected with barricades of any kind?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever, during 1992, 1993, and 1994, during that period of time, in that particular street in relation to the students hostel, both of them, did you ever see any barricades erected there?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you're saying, what you're telling us, is that you did not see, you never saw any barricades in the Alije Branko Bujic Street?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. Because we didn't dare walk around there, because there was some army there and we always avoided walking in that direction. And on that particular day, we got pretty close and we got what we got.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that on the 6th of May, 2001, you gave a statement to the investigators of the Prosecution? Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which year did you say?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what statement you mean. You would have to tell me what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is the statement which you gave on the 6th of May while talking to the investigators of the Prosecution. That's the one I mean. Do you remember talking to some people who introduced themselves as such on the 6th of May, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think so. I can't remember the exact date, but that I gave a statement, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that everything you said in your statement is correct and true? Everything you told the investigators of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I read portions of your statement to you, would you be able to confirm that they are true? And I'm going to quote a passage from your statement dated the 6th of May. It is Document 0302-27638, and it is paragraph 5 on page 2 of the B/C/S version. "We used to take walks in this way before and we never thought that somebody was going to shoot us there. It wasn't sheltered from the snipers, but we hadn't been shot at before in this spot. The front line was about 200 metres away." Is that correct what I've just read out?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that particular day, the day that you say you cannot actually say what day it was exactly, but that you think it was April, can you give us the year? What year do you think it was?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, whether it was 1993 perhaps or -- well, I assume it was 1993, but I can't say for certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that the three of you were walking abreast, in a line abreast. You were one next to the other?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, abreast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, at the time the two of your friends were hit, that is to say Mr. Franjic and Vucic, what position were they in at that moment? Because you said that you had given assistance to both of them, so what position were they in?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were on the pavement abreast of each other, walking in a line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Can you tell us, at the time the two of your friends were hit, Ivan Franjic, that is, and the late Vucic, what position were they in when you were trying to help them? How far away from each other were they when they were hit and you were helping them?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were on the pavement, all of us, so we were all next to each other, body up against body, right next to each other. I can't say exactly, but I think we were touching each other, sort of next to each other, one body next to another, and walking that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you confirm, and I think that you said that during the examination-in-chief, that you didn't hear the actual shots?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, we didn't hear them. We didn't feel anything until we were actually wounded, or they were wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us yesterday when my learned colleague was asking questions, and it was at 11.39, the time was 11.39, you said that a woman and a man helped you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, from the Ante Babica building, from that settlement, they saw the two men fall down. And I tried to help Ivan. I couldn't help the other one because he fell and asked for help, but I couldn't because I was busy with Franjic. And when I sent him off to Dobrinja, I tried to help Vucic, too. And I asked the people that were going by in a car to transport Vucic to hospital, but he didn't live for long afterwards. And he died. But the other man survived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Mr. Kapetanovic, you are confirming here and now that you personally helped both Mr. Franjic and the late Mr. Vucic, and that you sent them off in cars to hospitals, that you stopped the cars and had them transported?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, the man who helped you, the man who came out to help you, did he bring you a bandage, too?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, how was he dressed, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, he was just a simple civilian who came to help us. Whether he was on the ground floor in that building and saw the two men had fallen and that I was trying to help them - he must have seen that - and he brought some bandages and pieces of cloth so that we could bandage Franjic's stomach, as it had been shot through and his intestines were about to fall out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, after you helped your friends, and if you did, who did you report the incident to?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Truth to tell, I did not make any statements. But when I called Franjic's family, his wife and his daughter, I told them that this had happened, that he was in the hospital, and then perhaps on the basis of that, they tried to report it. I didn't report it anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, that day when the incident happened, did you have any contact with the police of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you that day at that time, as you walked, as you were having your walk, did you see in your immediate vicinity - and when I say your immediate vicinity, I mean yours and Mr. Franjic's and the late Augustin's - did you see any police?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see them. I did not see anyone in the vicinity. I would have sought their help had I seen anyone. I would have sought help, asked them to help my friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Franjic [sic], if I tell you that on the 18th of February, a policeman testified in this Court who claimed that he was the one who had helped late Augustin and Ivan, can you tell us if that is correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Franjic -- Kapetanovic. My apologies. The policeman who was -- who testified on the 18th of February, during the examination-in-chief before this Chamber, when asked by my learned friend, stated that he and a friend of his, who was also a policeman, had heard two shots.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear them, and I therefore cannot say that I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The gentleman policeman who testified said that with his friend, who was another policeman, had hailed a car, the first, and put in that car late Augustin first. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I tell you that this policeman stated that he had extended assistance to Ivan Franjic and hailed another car, taken his particulars and put him in the car, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember. The first car we stopped, we put Ivan in that car. And I believe it was a Golf, if I remember correctly. And we dispatched him to Dobrinja. And it was only then that we tried to hail another car so as to -- because Augustin had sustained more severe injury, and we were looking for another car to send him to Kosevo, and that is what we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are telling us that at the moment when both Ivan and late Vucic were injured, that no policeman was with you there?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see any. Perhaps there was one on the other side, but I did not see him. Perhaps. Perhaps there was somebody watching, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are telling us that the statement of a policeman who testified before this Chamber, that it was he and his friend, another policeman, who helped Ivan Franjic and late Augustincic [sic], that that is not correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not notice that. Perhaps at that moment, I was beside myself because I had suffered the stress and all this had happened. So I did not see him by then. Perhaps I simply wasn't myself right at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think I understood my learned colleague to put to this witness that Mr. Dziho gave evidence to this Trial Chamber on the 18th of February to the effect that the first of the men that they assisted was Augustin and the second was Ivan. I think that appears at page 23, line 3, in the English transcript. That's in relation to the proposition being put to the witness that the first person I assisted was Augustin. My friend then said, "Is that correct?" And the witness replied, "No, that is not correct. My friend then went on to say, in effect, that the second person assisted was Ivan Franjic. He then asked, "Is that correct?" And the witness replied, "I do not remember." I refer my friend to the transcript of the evidence of Mr. Dziho. The English transcript --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please refer to the page and the line, Mr. Ierace, so that I can follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Unfortunately, the only copy I have in hard copy refers to it as page 6, which is not the Microsoft Word copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but page 6 would be the sixth page from the beginning, so that helps me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On that page, Mr. Dziho talks about the first person they assisted, and then at line 7 he was asked: "Were you obtain from the man any information, including his name?" Page 11, he replies -- line 11, he replies, "Ivan Franjic." He goes on to explain that they stopped a car and put him in it. And line 21, he says that when the car left with this first injured person, he was then informed that there was another injured person. Mr. Dziho then attended that person, and going over the page, put him in a vehicle. And he was asked the name of that second person, and at line 18 on page 7, he says, "I think Augustin Vucic." So it seems that what my learned colleague has put to the witness is not only inconsistent with the evidence, at least at that point, but the opposite. And what she -- what appears in the transcript is, in fact, consistent with the recollection of the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I will resolve the problem by rephrasing the question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, can you tell us, of your two friends, the two friends who were injured that day, which one of them did you help first, stop the car to take him to the hospital? Was it Mr. Ivan or late Augustin?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Mr. Ivan Franjic, the first one. And only after that, after we had sent Ivan on his way, then we set out helping Vucic, because he was much more severely injured and he couldn't move.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I tell you that if Mr. Fuad Dziho, who testified on the 18th of February, stated that it was in the afternoon when they were present at the time of the incident, can you then tell us which of the two statements is correct, that it was in the morning as you said, or in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it was in the morning between 10.00 and 11.00. I cannot tell you the exact time, but it was thereabouts. That is what I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kapetanovic, you told us that you extended assistance to Mr. Ivan Franjic. You confirmed for us that at the moment when you were extending this help, that you did not see the policeman. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see him. That man who came up, I did not see him in a uniform, the one who helped. Whether he was a policeman or something, I don't know, but he was wearing civilian clothes, the man who helped me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you confirming to us that you bandaged the wound with a bandage that you were given, that you bandaged Ivan Franjic's wound?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't do it all by myself, but together with the man who helped me, the two of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are telling us that this man was in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, I will now show you the statement of Ivan Franjic, who was examined on the 21st of November, 1995, page 2 of translation in Serbian. The document is 0090-6702.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: My friend, according to the English transcript, has put to the witness that Mr. Franjic was examined on that date. He was not examined on that date, but he made a statement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's the way we understood it. Of course there was no Court session.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I said 21st of November, 1995, that he made his statement which I've already used, quoting from it. And I will quote again. Part of Mr. Ivan Franjic's statement which refers to that incident at the time when he was injured, he said -- so it is the fifth passage, line 4.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel read it slowly because the interpreters do not have the text. Could the counsel either please put the text on the ELMO or start again because the interpreters were not given this text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, could you either read it very slowly, since you did not provide the interpreters with a hard copy of what you're quoting, or put it on the ELMO so that they can follow it? I think if it's not too long, slow reading goes -- takes less time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will read it slowly. But Mr. Franjic, I gave Mr. Ivan Franjic's statement to interpreters team for all the three booths.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that is true, then of course I have to withdraw, yes. I see that it's confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But I'll read it now slowly: "And then some policemen ran up to me and noticed that I had been wounded. They bandaged my wound. They took me to a car, and then to the hospital at Dobrinja. I did not see either Augustin or Marko."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, can you confirm for us what is true?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's quite correct that he helped to bandage his wound and we put him in a car and asked the driver to take him to Dobrinja. That is correct. Did I see those policemen? I saw a man who helped me bandage him, but that was it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The witness has indeed already said that the man who provided assistance wasn't in a uniform. There is nothing in the passage that has been read to the witness from the statement of Ivan Franjic to the effect explicitly that the policeman was in a uniform. When my friend says to the witness, "which is correct," my friend should make clear to the witness if she is saying to the witness that Mr. Dziho was in a uniform, and if so, where does that evidence come from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, your question suggests that there was a contradiction between the statement given by Mr. Franjic and what the witness testified. As indicated by Mr. Ierace, that, as it stands now, is not the case. So for the reasons he gave, would you first clarify that before confronting the witness with a suggestion that there's a contradiction. Of course, we have not seen the whole statement of Mr. Franjic but what source makes him believe and what quality someone assisted him does not become clear from the part you read. So to that extent, the objection is sustained.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour -- Your Honour, when I asked him, the witness said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, perhaps we put off the earphones of Mr. Kapetanovic when you would like to add something. Ms. Philpott, could you please for a moment remove the headphones from Mr. Kapetanovic. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. During my cross-examination, Mr. Kapetanovic told us that in that part of the city, there were police and that the police had uniforms and that they invariably wore them. He also explained to us that policemen were uniformed persons. The second problem which arises is whether at the time when Ivan and Augustin were injured, there was somebody next to them. Yesterday, it was at 11.42 to 11.40, and he was asked whether there was anybody else besides there. The answer was no, nobody. Today, once again, when I asked him, he confirmed that there were no policemen in his presence. So the Defence takes it that the witness distinguishes between a person who is in uniform and a person who may be a policeman but is not wearing a uniform. Today, when asked, he confirmed once again that the person who gave him the bandage was a civilian, bearing in mind Mr. Franjic's statement given to OTP investigators, which I showed to Mr. Kapetanovic and who was very clear about it, "and then some policemen ran up to me and noticed that I had been wounded."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just interrupt you, the contradiction seems to be, in your view, that where Mr. Franjic identifies the person as a policeman, that this witness does not. But the statement of Mr. Franjic gives no information, as far as it has been read to us, as far as how he knew that this was a policeman. It could have been told to him on the way to hospital. It could have been told to him later. So that's the first observation I make. The second observation is that wasn't the testimony of Mr. Dziho that he was a reserve policeman, who was not belonging to the police forces before the war. I think he was then a social worker or something like that. And that he then as a reserve policeman joined the police force, which, of course, may be of relevance as far as the conclusions you're drawing from the testimony of the witness, that policemen would wear uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The reserve --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore the contradiction, as you suggested to the witness, does not follow from what you've read, neither does it follow from the testimony the witness has been given until now. That's the reason why I asked to you to clarify the issue first before putting any suggestion that there's a contradiction between the statement of Mr. Franjic and the testimony of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, all I have to say is that Mr. Dziho during the examination-in-chief and testimony before this Tribunal said that the reserve police force had uniforms. Therefore, Mr. Dziho confirmed for us that the reserve police force wore uniforms and he also confirmed that he had been issued with a semi-automatic rifle which he always had with him. I do not have the transcript before me, and I therefore cannot quote you exactly the part of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just see whether there's any talk about uniforms in the statement of Mr. Dziho. One moment, please. Would that be on the 18th of February?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My search on the word "uniform" on the 18th of February doesn't give any result. But of course it might be that the ... Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I also had conducted a search with the same negative result. I note the time, and my point is simply, as you have expressed, that he was a reserve policeman. I don't recollect at this point whether he said anything about the wearing of uniforms or not. Perhaps in the interest of saving time, we could check during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps that's a good suggestion. Let me just see whether the evidence of Mr. Dziho continued on the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may take the liberty, what I find here, are we talking about the page 3800 onward? Referring to the statement of the 18th of February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just check. The testimony of Mr. Dziho starts -- let me just have a look. On the 18th of February, we first had another witness and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because we see the word "uniform," but in English, it seems that it is in plural. Excuse me, let me check my system here. I'll find it. What I found, I found this word "uniform" in plural, line 14 on page 3880, but we shall continue searching.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But the testimony of Mr. Dziho commences on page 3901, so if there was --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will check that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- On the pages before, it must have been for other witnesses. If you would please check that during the break, then I'll first get in touch with Sarajevo again. At least with Mr. Kapetanovic. Ms. Philpott, could you please put the headphones back again. Mr. Kapetanovic, we had a small legal technical problem, and we'll try to resolve that during the break, during the next half an hour. So your cross-examination will be resumed by counsel for the Defence at 11.00, and we'll have a break until then. If I may invite the parties -- Ms. Philpott, if you'd please escort the witness out of the videoroom. Then, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The line is 3921 to 25 -- [In English] line is 25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] 3921, the line is 25. And here it seems we could find the word "uniforms" in English, with a plural, "S."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see it in the plural. Usually my computer also gives a result if I ask for the ... I see the word "uniform" in relation ... "That was after 1992, and what kind of weapons did you have?" "I had a long barrel, ammunition, and uniforms." That's what I read on this line. I'd like to have a look at it in the context of the whole testimony, and if we all use the break for that, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll then have a break until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in the interests of saving time, I withdraw the objection. Secondly, in relation to what my learned colleague, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, said this morning, just briefly on that topic, the other day the Prosecution handed up the two original documents of the letter of discharge. Mr. President, if they are still with you, might they be returned to the Prosecution so that we can arrange for the retranslations to be done. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean to say the original copies of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. They may be returned to you. We didn't have a look at it, to be quite honest, until now. One is a -- it seems to be approximately the same document as before. Madam Registrar, would you please give it to the usher so that -- yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I fear that I have been misunderstood once again by the Prosecution. That was probably because I didn't express myself properly. Not to have the documents retranslated, but to tell us why one document does not contain what it contains in the other. So the translations plus the explanation, that will be what I will be waiting for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I didn't understand that this was the response of the Prosecution. So let's just first wait until they give some kind of an explanation, and let's then see whether there's any need to continue any debate on that. Well, since your objections have been withdrawn, Ms. Pilipovic, I think we could resume the cross-examination. Let me just confer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, to avoid whatever misunderstanding, the Chamber expects an explanation rather soon, let me say it this way; I would say one of the coming days.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, because the translation was done by the translation, which as I understand it is not part of the OTP, it will be necessary for us to, in turn, make an inquiry of the translation unit as to how that translation could have come in the form that it did. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that was my understanding as well, that you need some time to investigate what actually happened. Ms. Pilipovic, I see you're ready to resume the cross-examination, or do you want to bring anything else to the attention of the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence is just concerned, because of the time that is being taken from the cross-examination with objections and comments from my learned colleague, and I think time is valuable to us. We have wasted quite a bit of time discussing the objection, but I am ready for the cross-examination to continue. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, of course we'll always consider the actual way the examination or cross-examination was done. But I'm glad that the Defence is well aware of how objections can damage the course of an examination. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic. We'll first check whether the witness is in the videoroom in Sarajevo. Ms. Philpott, could you please escort the witness into the videoroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, counsel for the Defence will continue cross-examining you. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, before the break, I was referring to the statement by Mr. Ivan Franjic, and from it we were able to conclude that Mr. Ivan Franjic in his statement states that he did not see you at the point at which he was wounded. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I assisted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In spite of my reluctance to object, I must object to that question. That is not the evidence -- that is not the contents of the passage of Mr. Franjic's statement that was read to the witness. Mr. Franjic did not in that passage say that he did not see Mr. Kapetanovic at the point at which he was wounded. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, the lines you read -- I will try to find them. Just trying to find the lines where you're quoting the statement of Mr. Franjic. I found it. I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You read to the witness: "And then some policemen ran up to me and noticed that I had been wounded. They bandaged my wound. They took me to a car, and then to the hospital in Dobrinja. I did not see either Augustin or Marko."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps the witness might remove his headphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Philpott, could you please remove the headphones from Mr. Kapetanovic. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: My learned colleague well knows that in the preceding paragraphs of Mr. Franjic's statement, the account is given that the three men were walking together "when I was shot." And therefore to put this proposition to the witness is not only contrary to the passage that was read, but contrary to the contents of the statement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we may start out from the premise that the three people were walking and that Mr. Franjic said that in his statement. Now, we come to the witness's credibility, Mr. Kapetanovic's in fact, at the point in time when both these two men were injured, wounded, whether he was present, especially in view of Dziho Fuad's testimony who was heard before this Tribunal. He made no mention during his testimony or in his statement that Mr. Marko was in fact present. And during my cross-examination, I did ask Mr. Marko whether he contacted on that day with any official and whether he reported the incident to anybody. So the question arises as to whether Mr. Marko was actually present at the actual time, at the material time, when Mr. Ivan and Mr. Augustin were injured. So we have to ascertain who is telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What my learned colleague has said fails completely to respond to my objection, which is simply that she has misrepresented the statement of Mr. Franjic to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic, as far as we understand, without having read the statement of Mr. Franjic, and since you did not deny a part of the factual basis of the objection of Mr. Ierace, I do understand that the statement of Mr. Franjic says that they were walking together, the three men, but that at least at a later stage, after he said he was taken to Dobrinja hospital, "I didn't see the other two." So we have three stages. The first is the moment of walking before the incident; then the incident and the assistance; and then the later stage where those injured or killed were taken away from the spot of the incident. Would you please make quite clear in your questioning to the witness, and also if you're referring to other statements or other testimony, what moment you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And to that extent, the objection is sustained. Ms. Philpott, could you please replace the headphones for Mr. Kapetanovic. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Kapetanovic, at the moment when Ivan and Augustin were wounded, at that particular moment, do you confirm that you, yourself, helped Ivan, gave assistance to Ivan, and that you bandaged his wound? Do you confirm that? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I put it to you that Mr. Ivan said that some policeman ran up to him and noticed that he was wounded and bandaged his wound, what would you say was true? Is what you're telling us the truth, or is what we see in the statement of the 21st of November, 1995, as stated by Mr. Franjic true? Who dressed or bandaged his wound?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that a man in civilian clothing came up who helped me bandage Ivan Franjic's wound. That is the truth. I can't say something that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to have the witness shown the 360-degree electronically-joined photograph, 3280U. It is the Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think we need the assistance of the case manager. I see that she is preparing. Ms. Philpott, could you please confirm when the not-yet moving part of the 360-degrees photograph appears on your screen in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] We do have the image now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I couldn't hear you, Ms. Philpott.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] We have the image on the screen now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, can you see part of the Alija Branko Bujic Street, and looking at it from the right-hand side, you can see the students hostel.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. You would have to zoom in towards the right for the Branko Bujic Street to be visible.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you pan it, please, to the right. Thank you. Stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is that the beginning of the Alija Branko Bujic Street?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kapetanovic, can you tell us, please, the elevation that can be seen at the end of the street, looking at it from our angle of vision? Could you tell us what part of town that is? Is that Buljatov Potok?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be, but it's lower down. Buljakov Potok and the lower part of Buljakov Potok, it is to my right as I look at the screen, a little lower down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And What about the hilly part, the elevation, what's that called, if you can say?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that hill -- I've forgotten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it Brijesce Brdo or Brijesce hill?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Brijesce Brdo is a higher hill joining this elevation, but I can't remember the name of this particular elevation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you -- do you claim or can you tell us that this -- whether this part, the one that we see on the photograph that you said the lower part of which is Buljakov Potok, that that part of town was under the control of the BH army. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't claim that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we now pan further to the right in the direction of Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other way around, the reserve. Pan backwards and then go to Branko Bujic Street. A little more. A bit more. That's it. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we go right again to see the direction of the street?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, a little more to the right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if the Defence might be permitted, may we ask the technicians to pan to the right so that we have Alija Branko Bujic Street on our screens?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can ask those who are technically assisting us to the right or to the left, but not to specific streets --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A little more to the right then. Right, please. A bit more, please. Right. [In English] Stop. [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, is this Alija Branko Bujic Street and the direction you were moving in towards Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, can you confirm that in the buildings that we see to your left, on the left-hand side of the screen, that those are buildings which belonged to Alipasino Polje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that in the buildings that we see on the left-hand side, the first buildings, on the ground floor where the office premises were, that soldiers of the BH army were located there?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we now pan to the right again, further to the right, please. Stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kapetanovic, looking at this photograph, can you confirm the fact that this part of the street in which you would be moving towards Dobrinja is at a higher elevation compared -- is higher than the part of the building which is, in fact, the students centre? Is the road or street slightly raised?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is a little raised, a little higher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, we're looking at the students hostel building. Can you tell us, during the conflict in 1992, 1993, and 1994, who used the building? Who was the building used by? Do you happen to know that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. But all I know is that there were no students there at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know that the army was in that building?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that in the -- on the building where we see the windows looking at us, facing us, that on the other side of the building opposite these windows, there are also buildings and rooms facing the other way?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you answer the following: In view of the fact that you have confirmed the existence of damages on this building - you have said that - how was the building damaged and how were the buildings damaged, looking at the building from our angle of vision?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the building, the opposite side of the building, you said that there were windows on that opposite side, too, and rooms as well, that that other opposite side of the building was damaged, too. Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was damaged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you confirm that on this building, both the windows facing us and the windows facing the other side were all damaged?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you also confirm that the walls of this building facing the other side where you say there were windows, that the walls were damaged, too?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, partially. Not very much, but yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "partially," what part of the building were the walls damaged, looking at the side of the building that we see on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the other side of the building, the opposite side. You could see some damage on the opposite side of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the side we're facing, facing us, was there any damage there?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was just the windows that were damaged. The windows were shattered, the glass was broken of the windows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you're saying this side, this side that we're facing, it's only the windows that were broken and not the walls?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, not the walls. As we could see it, the walls were not damaged. But on the opposite side, the wall was damaged, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you saw that later on, when was it that you saw it? Was it in 1992, 1993, 1994, within that time frame or after that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are confirming for us that in late 1993, you saw broken windows on this building?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are confirming that the walls of this building were not damaged, are you?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, I do not think we saw any damage done to those walls. But I wasn't particularly keen on establishing that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We should like to show the witness 3279OA, please. Can we have that shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you like to be shown in Sarajevo or -- Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Philpott, could you please assist us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] I believe that is Prosecution number P3279OB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
