utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic, there is a marked copy available in Sarajevo, in colour, at this moment. I don't know whether the marking bothers you or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, then. Yes, Your Honour. I just have one more question while we still have this photograph on the screen. The witness can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, can you see these cars and vehicles there?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have this photograph any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Philpott, there is one additional question by Ms. Pilipovic concerning the 360-degrees photograph. Could you please confirm that that is on the screen in front of Mr. Kapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] We now have it on the screen again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, these vehicles and these cars and trucks that are here, do they hide from view the street leading to military cemetery, Vojnicko Polje and Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right here, right now, they do. But they are not always there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are confirming that behind these trucks in the direction of the students hostel, there is a street leading towards Vojnicko Polje and Nedzarici. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the name of that street?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Branko Bujic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like the photograph 3279 to be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Philpott, could you please put on the ELMO in Sarajevo P3279OB. That is the colour version. Ms. Pilipovic, I see that it is on the ELMO in Sarajevo. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Now, if the photograph can be zoomed off so that we have the whole photograph. Can it be zoomed off so that we can see the whole photograph? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you indicate on this photograph the place where you were at the moment when Mr. Ivan and Mr. Augustin and you, in your belt, as you say, were hit?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please use the black marker to mark the spot where you were standing.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you make a circle and write number 1.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, during the direct examination, is that the place where you tell us today that is the place where you were standing?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the transcript, the witness has marked on the photograph a circle and put "1" in Alija Branko Bujic Street at the bottom of this photograph, in the middle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the sake of the record, Ms. Pilipovic, we can see, and if the document will be admitted in evidence, everyone will see where the circle and the "1" is. On what street it is, is of course not -- is a different question. So I think as soon as there's a clear marking on a photograph, for the sake of the transcript, it's not necessary to indicate that. Describing where someone is pointing at is of importance, since there are no traces remaining. But if it's not marked, it's not necessary, and it's especially not necessary to add something which is not visible, and that is the name of the street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, at that spot which you have just marked and as the spot where you were at that point in time, are you confirming for us that all three of you were right there at that time?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, at the time when you were injured, how far were you away from the pedestrian crossing?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been about 10 metres perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, from the direction, from the place that you marked as a place where you were injured, that is, that Mr. Ivan and late Augustin sustained the injuries, can you take a pencil, draw a line to mark the direction from which, as you say, you assume that the shots were fired?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you take the marker to indicate the direction to, as you say, blind people's home, because you said you assumed that the shots had been fired from there.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And further on, Mr. Kapetanovic, right up to the place which you said was the blind people's home.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic -- just a moment. Let me see.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the whole photograph on the ELMO. Can it be zoomed off so that we have the whole photograph. And a bit further off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in the right corner of the photograph, we see a crossing, a pedestrian crossing. Is that correct? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the corner, in the right corner of the photograph at the bottom, we also see a roof of a building which you, yesterday, when asked by my learned friend, showed to us and identified as the roof belonging to that small building on the corner. Can you point at this part of the roof at the bottom of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking at the bottom of the photograph, to the right. Right down at the bottom to the right, where the pedestrian crossing is. At the bottom of the photograph, Mr. Kapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Right. Right where the corner of the photograph is. Far right, where you have a car. Move right, and further on and down, right, down, at the bottom. Mr. Kapetanovic, at the bottom of the photograph. Can you hear me? Right down at the bottom of the photograph, there is a pedestrian crossing. Right down there. There is a pedestrian crossing. Mr. Kapetanovic, down there at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Is that the pedestrian crossing that you crossed to proceed with your walk down Branko Bujic Street?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But we were not having our walk along Branko Bujic Street. We were walking along Ante Babica Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My apology. But is that the pedestrian crossing that you crossed?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. At the bottom, to the left, when you move to the left, can you see the roof of a building which is there on the corner? Can you see that roof down there? You identified it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right down there. Next to that pedestrian crossing that you marked as the -- at the crossing that you had crossed. Right down there at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, you indicated yesterday that this was the spot where you were at the moment when fire was opened on you. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not there. But where I marked the place as number 1, that is where we were, on the pavement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, yesterday, on the videotape that my colleague -- that my learned friend showed you during his examination, where you stood and marked as a place which was marked in yellow as a place where you were standing at the moment when you were hit, and that is the place as you crossed the pedestrian crossing where this small building is, and it is in the videotape. We can show that tape to you.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photo, yes, that tape shows it best. The tape on which I point at the place where we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I tell you that the place which you now pointed at where this small building is, will you agree -- will you confirm that it is the house that you see on the videotape?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right in front of that small building is where that happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you then mark the place where you see the roof where that small building is at the bottom of the photograph. Can you mark it.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you put number 2 there, please, just above that roof.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, can you, in relation to that place which you have just marked with number 2 and which you indicated on the videotape as the place where you were standing, can you indicate the direction from which the shots were fired at the moment when your friends were injured? And will you draw a line towards the blind people's home from this spot, from number 2.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot do this because I do not know if the bullets came directly from there. We didn't -- since we didn't hear the shots or anything, we only knew that we were hit. Secondly, I cannot claim from where that bullet reached us. I cannot really affirm that with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are telling us that you do not know from which direction the shots were fired?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my assumption that they came from the blind people's home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in relation to number 2 that you had just marked, can you draw a line in the direction of the blind people's home if we assume that, in relation to the place number 2, the shots were fired from the blind people's home. Can you draw a line in the direction of the blind people's home? From point number 2.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I'd just like to put to the parties that I fully understand what your line of questioning is. I would have expected a different line as well. We all had a line in our mind, I would say, as an answer to that question. I think the Chamber has to establish that this witness is not able to give consistent answers on questions in relation to these -- to this photograph. If any of the parties would disagree, I'd like to know now so that I would be in a position to give it some reflection and to see what to do. But I think it's rather useless. And since the examination of witnesses is under the guidance of the Chamber, I'd just suggest that we not continue any more, not because your questions are not important, but just because everyone may have noticed now that answers to these questions are rather inconsistent. I see Mr. Ierace is nodding as agreeing. This would be just as well as this we were talking about yesterday, Mr. Ierace, as you might notice.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. In that vein, the Defence will ask a question regarding Photograph 3 -- 3280, and we have this one other question to the witness, and then a few more questions, and that will be the end of our cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please then proceed. The next --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, Mr. Kapetanovic, do you see this photograph with cars and a truck?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're talking about the 360 degrees? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, now, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, in the lower part of the photograph, the far right corner of the photograph, do you see a building?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, so that there is not confusion at a later point, perhaps I could just clarify the exhibit number of the electronic photograph. My friend identified it as 3280. In fact, it's 327U. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please then proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, at the bottom of this photograph, at the far right end, do you see a building in the distance?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But if you can move -- pan to the right. If you can move the photograph to the right, please. Stop. Now, on this photograph, in the direction of the pedestrian crossing straight ahead, can you see a building in the distance?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do. Can you confirm whether this is the Oslobodjenje building?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the Oslobodjenje building during the conflict, 1992, 1993, 1994, was controlled by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you -- do you have any knowledge about the police guarding this building throughout the conflict in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kapetanovic, can you tell us what colour were the jackets, the windjammers, that you were wearing that day, you and your friends on that day?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot say. It was just plain clothes. Whatever jackets we had, we wore. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said then that at that time -- at that time, a cease-fire had been signed. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never claimed that, and I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you. The Defence has concluded its cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, does the Prosecution want to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, but very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed. Mr. Kapetanovic, some more questions will be put to you now by counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace. Re-examined by Mr. Ierace:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, during the questioning by my learned colleague, she referred to Alija Branko Bujic Street. Is that the same street as Ante Babica Street, or is that a different street?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean it is not the same street as Ante Babica Street?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, what street were you on when you and your two friends were shot at and two of your friends were wounded?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Ante Babica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown Photograph 3279OB, I think it now is. That is the photograph in Sarajevo, from above.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I indicated to the Defence that questioning on the basis of this photograph is a very difficult exercise. I don't know what you're going to ask the witness about it, but could you please save us from getting into the same trouble again while questioning the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see on the photograph Ante Babica Street?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please point to it.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness indicates the street which runs parallel to the bottom of the photograph. The street is positioned along the bottom of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, do you see anywhere in the photograph Alija Branko Bujic Street?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness indicates street which intersects the street identified as Ante Babica Street and runs parallel to the left side of the photograph. Thank you. No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Mr. Kapetanovic, you gave your answers to all the questions of both Prosecution and Defence. The Judges have no further questions to you any more. I'd like to thank you very much for coming not only once but even on a second day to come and testify and give information to the parties and to the Chamber. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Philpott, the witness may be escorted out of the videoroom in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, did I well understand that your next witness will be Fatima Pita? That's the change of order you indicated before.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Philpott, in Sarajevo, if you could hear me, you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. could escort the next witness Fatima Pita into the videoroom. Meanwhile, we'll tender the documents from the witness. Madam Registrar, would you please guide us. Part of the documents shown were already admitted in evidence. But the new exhibits are -- yes, could you please name them and describe them so that we can take a decision. I think the first one is P3202. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It is P3202, and that is a map showing a red cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, a map marked with a red cross.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's admitted in evidence. Yes, next one.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next one is P3280U, which is the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's admitted in evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next exhibit is P3265. That is a photograph depicting buildings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Also admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P3279U, which is the CD-Rom electronic 360-degree photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's also admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The last one I have is P3279B, which is the annotated version of P3279OA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's also -- yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, simply to indicate the Defence always has the same objections, the objections put forward with respect to the electronically-joined exhibits, especially as in this case the witness gave at least three possible locations as the material spot where the incident took place. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The standing objection against the 360-degrees photographs is taken into consideration every time we take a decision on this type of material. So 3279OB is also admitted into evidence. Ms. Philpott, may I just address you. Would you bring to The Hague the Exhibit P3279OB which is marked in Sarajevo. I take it that you'll keep it in your custody until returning to The Hague. Thank you very much for that. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, but before we hear the next witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness is standing and waiting. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just briefly, with respect to the testimony of this witness, we would have liked to have received the military documents that we discussed a little while ago. We don't have them. The Defence is once again handicapped by those -- that particular fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take notice of your remark, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Ms. Philpott, I see the headphones are placed on the head of the next witness. Mrs. Pita, welcome, I cannot say in this courtroom, but welcome at least in the videoroom where we can see you. I expect that you can see us on your screen as well and that you can hear me in a language --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to you, Your Honours, and hello from sunny Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for the sunshine you bring to The Hague, Ms. Pita. Before testifying in this Court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. And the text of this declaration is being handed to you now by the representative of the Registry. May I invite you to make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Pita. Please be seated. Ms. Pita, the order is that you'll first be examined by counsel for the Prosecution, then by counsel for the Defence, and if there are any additional questions the Judges would like to put to you, you'll hear from them. Mr. Ierace, you may start.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Ierace:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your name Fatima Pita?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, were you living in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you live there throughout the armed conflict between 1992 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you living there by the end of -- withdraw that. Were you living there in December 1992?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that stage, were you married, in December 1992?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any children in December 1992?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many children did you have?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What are the names of those two children, and what sex?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Two girls. The eldest one's name is Selma, and the younger one is Anisa. Anisa, sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old were they in December 1992?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Selma was born on the 27th of March, 1975. And let me just emphasise, Your Honour, that my older daughter is from a previous marriage. Anisa was born on the 16th of June, 1989, and it was from my second marriage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts in Sarajevo were you living in December 1992?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I was living in Stari Grad Zadrici Street number 38.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that address, during the armed conflict, up until December 1995, had there been any shells landing near your place?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes. Every day, like drops of rain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the armed conflict, was your daughter Anisa wounded?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: On the 13th of December, 1992, between 10.00 and 11.00 in the forenoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had there been any shelling near your place either that morning or the night before or a few days before?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: The previous night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you during the shelling?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: We were, my family and I, were a little -- and some of the neighbours, were in my basement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your husband, yourself, and your two children, and some neighbours, were in your basement during the shelling the night before. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many shells did you hear falling in the area the night before from your basement?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: The previous night, that is to say on the 12th of December, that night from the first evening hours until 5.00 in the morning, I counted a full 70 shells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What condition was your residence in on the morning of the 13th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: The house, as a house, is an old building, it's an old house. But the house is slightly on an incline, on a hill, so that the basement or cellar was in concrete, although the entrance door to the cellar were not as protected. They, too, were exposed like the door up above.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What condition was your house in on the morning of the 13th of December, 1992, in terms of cleanliness?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: It was in a poor state. It had been hit with five shells. Two dropped on the roof. Luckily, those two didn't explode. But all the others fell around the house, around the gate, and that morning, when things became quieter, I went outside. Because in our cellar or basement, there wasn't a toilet or anything else, so we would have to go upstairs two at a time or three at a time. And I found the door leading into the living room all broken down. There was -- there were bricks and bits of steel and everything else, earth and so on. Now, I have a flower bed right in front of my door. Everything had been -- there was a detonation, an explosion, and it was all scattered about inside the house and you couldn't recognise it at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any military positions near your house at that time?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you live in an area that was on the Bosnian government side of the confrontation lines or on the other side of the confrontation lines at that time?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I don't know what sides there were, left or right. I think it should have right, below Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is whether -- withdraw that. My question is on what side of the confrontation lines was your house? Was it on the side of the Bosnian government forces or on the other side?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: On the Serb side, there were forces of the Serb army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean by that that you and your family lived on the Serb side of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: We lived -- it was our territory, but behind us were the Serb positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Mrs. Pita, did you understand during the war that the forces that controlled the city, the main part of the city, were the armed forces of the Bosnian government? Was that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, I have an objection to make. I do apologise. Despite my reluctance to object, I have to make an objection here because when we're talking about the city, we have seen that there are different parts of the city that were divided into different factions and could, therefore, Mr. Ierace specify what faction and what quarter he is referring to, what district. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid I can't hear very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ierace, since Mr. Piletta-Zanin does not understand or at least is of the opinion that it might not be clear to the witness, would you please rephrase the question. But it's not necessary to indicate all the specific parts of the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I had in fact been careful to refer to the main part of the city, but I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Pita --

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- you referred a few moments ago to the Serb side of the confrontation line. Was that your side or the other side?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you answered "yes," so I'll rephrase the question again. How far was your house from the confrontation lines in December 1992, approximately? Approximately how far?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: This is how I can clarify matters: On that hill, there's a rock that we call "Baba," and that's where my daughter was hit from. Before the war, I was there several times on this hill for a picnic. There's a lovely view of Sarajevo, and we would gather there from time to time. I think, but I can't specify, I'm not an expert, but between 200 and 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which forces controlled Baba on the day that your daughter was wounded?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes, that was the Baba rock, and between that Baba rock, there was a road controlled by Serb forces. In between the two rocks, this road went between the two rocks. One rock was higher up and one rock was a little lower down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could listen to my question carefully, please. Which forces actually controlled Baba on the day that your daughter was wounded? Was it the Serb forces --

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, coming back to the morning of the 13th of December, you've told us about the condition of your house. Did you have running water at that time, water coming through the taps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have to intervene because the question, the question to which -- in which the term was used "Serb forces," this question is a leading question in which Serb forces are referred to and, therefore, it is unacceptable as being a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in fact, the question I asked was not leading. And whilst the witness was answering the questions, I started to ask a further question which would have posed alternative forces. I got as far as saying "Serb forces" when the witness interrupted me. So on the transcript, it may appear that there was a leading question, whereas in fact there was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is indicated on the transcript, there are two, not dots, but two -- and it is also my recollection that you were interrupted by the witness, who did not wait to give an answer. So please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Pita, did you have water in your taps, coming out of your taps, on the 13th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No, we didn't. From 1992 onwards, I personally, and I think the whole city, but I'm talking about my house and my household, we had no water, no electricity, no telephone. All that was cut off. I think it was cut off on one and the same day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did someone obtain water that morning?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes. On the 12th of December, that morning, I was the first to get up. Everybody else got up, too, because believe me, Your Honours, if you haven't got any electricity and you have no water and no food and no contact with anything, then you can't sleep for long. So we would go to bed early and get up very early, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the 13th of December, which I think you said was the date that your daughter was wounded. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: My husband and my little girl went to fetch water, that night, on the 12th, in the evening. There was a little rain, and we were happy because that was a source of water, and the streams would rise. It wasn't drinking water, but for hygiene purposes and in the home for cleaning. Mountain streams would rise when it rained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time was it when your husband and your little girl went to fetch water?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: They went -- I can't specify the time. Perhaps it was about 8.00, or between 8.00 and 9.00. My husband took the canisters, and my little girl had a small can of her own. It might have been a 5 litre can. She was with her father. She liked her father. So that the two of them went off to fetch water to the stream, to the creek. It wasn't -- there wasn't a lot of water there, just dribbles of water, and there were quite a few people there so you had to wait in line, in a queue. And came back ten minutes later; her father stayed on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you refer to your little girl, do you mean Anisa?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes, I was referring to my daughter Anisa. Anisa came back at that -- where the water was, she found a girl that was four or five years older than her, and they came back to play. They came back to play, because that night there was a lot of shelling, and in the morning it was a little quieter. Now, the weather, it was foggy, a dull day, and we used that when visibility wasn't very good during the night, we went out looking for food, for firewood and so on. Now, when she came back, her friend had slippers on her feet. And at that point, at that moment, my little girl stepped in --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Pita, could you please --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There was interference, the interpreters note.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: She began doing up -- undoing her shoes, her laces, and you could hear shots. I was half a metre away from my girl when she hit. What you could see first was dust, and she screamed, and as she was taking off her shoes, her head fell on the threshold of the door, and she was huddled up. She didn't lie flat. She was huddled up and kneeling down, and she opened her mouth wide when she was hit, and I thought she had been mortally wounded. I didn't see any blood around her. I didn't see that she was hit in her head, but I felt ill myself, and I was screaming so loudly that all the neighbours came rushing to see what was going on. I wasn't conscious, Your Honours. And even to this day, Your Honours, I don't remember whether I brought her into the sitting room in my unconscious state or semiconscious state, or somebody else did that. But it was all a split second. It all happened in a split second, and I came to when they threw water over me and they said, "She's all right, she's all right, she wasn't hit in the head; she's been hit in the leg." And then I fainted again. When I saw that she had lived, survived, that it wasn't that bad, I fainted again. And I came to, I regained consciousness, and realised that I had to carry her myself and look for help to prevent her from bleeding to death. At that point, somebody told my husband up at the watering place that his daughter had been injured. He rushed back, brought back the water he managed to capture, 5 or 6 liters, and we used that -- they used that water to throw the water over us. And then after that, I turned round, looking for something to bandage her wound with. When we cut off her trousers, we saw that she had in fact been hit in her leg. There wasn't much blood. I saw the wound personally. And I looked at the trace the bullet had made from the threshold to her leg. It was an entrance/exit wound. We took off a pillow case. We had nothing else clean in the house because everything was dirty, and we used the white pillow case to bandage the wound. And my husband and my brother-in-law carried our little girl to the clinic. I don't know which route we took, but we reached the clinic, the health clinic, and they didn't have that many bandages either, but they bandaged her wound with the bandages they had, put a plaster on, and told her that it had to be operated because it was a entrance/exit wound, and that we should take her to Kosevo hospital, to the orthopaedic department. But we had no means of transportation so we carried her there. Shooting started in this place between the two buildings which was called Mejtas, and you could see it. It was a visible place, an exposed place. And we took her to the clinic, to the hospital. They admitted us, and at the hospital, there were a lot of people. There was a crowd. We went through the door. But I remember at that particular moment there was a doctor there. She was a foreigner, and she was a Bulgarian lady doctor. And she admitted us. They took our daughter in the operating theatre, examined her, told us to leave the room. We went out and I felt faint again but they said everything would be fine, that they had to treat the wound, to operate it, and then they came out and said, "There's no room here. You'll have to bring in your girl seven to ten days to have her wound dressed." So they didn't have any anaesthesia or any injections. They tended to her wound. They put a drainage system on her wound to ensure drainage to the wound, and my husband and I had to take her in every morning. I can't tell you how many kilometres it was but it was from one hill to the other. We took her every morning for her wound to be dressed. All I can tell you is that my little girl was not a very heavy little girl, she was just 9 kilos, but it's very difficult when you have to take shelter behind buildings to see whether you would be able to reach the hospital to have her wound dressed and whether you would be able to get back home alive, the three of us going there and back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Pita, you said that when you took her to the health clinic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't wish to interrupt the witness, and I didn't take the floor earlier, but in respect of what happened on page 66, line 6 of the transcript, as far as I can see it in English, there was a substantial difference in the French transcript and the English transcript. I thought I heard "she was one or one and a half metres from us," whereas in the English transcript I see "I was." It says "I." I think this is important to see whether the witness was speaking about herself or her friend. Because there is a difference between the French and English transcript. Thank you. I was listening to the French booth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, as a matter of fact we see that at that same spot, page 66, line 5, Mr. Ierace, there was interference. We also could see it on the screen since the image was not moving any more. I didn't want to interrupt either. Could you perhaps take the witness back to that very moment so in order to clarify what the answer was when the transmission seemed to be interfered by whatever technical.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Pita, whilst you gave that long account, there was an interruption in the --

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was an interruption in what we could hear.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I'll repeat. Let me repeat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please don't repeat. We heard everything you said except for approximately 8 seconds. I will tell you where that period of time was. You told us that the weather was a foggy -- in relation to the weather, it was a foggy, dull day, and you said these words: "And we used that when visibility wasn't very good. During the night, we went out looking for food, for firewood, and so on. When she came back, her friend had slippers on her feet. And at that point, at that moment, my little girl stepped in." And the next thing we heard you say, Mrs. Pita, was this: "She began doing up her laces and you could hear shots. I was half a metre away from my girl when she hit. What you could see first was dust, and she screamed." So Mrs. Pita, there was a period of a few seconds that we missed. Do you remember what it was you said in those few seconds? I remind you that we have you saying, "At that point, at that moment, my little girl stepped in -- "

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes, let me explain this a bit. It wasn't my friend. That girl, the girl with whom my daughter came was her friend. It was my daughter's friend. That little girl was five years old, and my daughter Anisa was three and a half years old. So it's her little girl, her friend, and they were coming back from the water to play in our house, or rather in our basement. So it wasn't my colleague or my friend. I apologise to the Court. Perhaps I wasn't clear enough. Made the mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now please wait one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, should I continue questioning now or later, given the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't want to obscure the debate, but may I be of assistance and help my learned colleague. Who was there? That's the question. Who was a metre and a half or half a metre from the child? That's the point, Mr. Ierace. Because we had this difference in transcripts. We know that it was the friend of the daughter. We understood that, all of us. But who was at a metre and a half or one and a half metres from the daughter when the accident took place? That's where the Gordian knot lies.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I had proposed to ask those questions of the witness, but the first step was simply to, in a neutral way, invite the witness to fill in the gap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think that the gap has been -- at least a few seconds might not have lost, of course. We do not know exactly what has been said. But I get the impression that we could proceed even without pointing very specifically on these six seconds. So perhaps keeping in mind the issue raised by Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you could proceed, Mr. Ierace. Apart from that, I look at the clock. Perhaps we might take a break now. As I indicated before, it will be a longer break than usual. Mrs. Pita, we'll have a break for approximately half an hour. That means that after this half an hour, the counsel for the Prosecution will resume examining you as a witness, and then of course the Defence counsel will come later. So we'll resume in half an hour and have a break until then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, are you...?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I want to bring to your attention that I spoke to the interpreters, or one of the interpreters, in particular, this morning, who indicated that the degree of interference with the voice line to Sarajevo makes it extremely difficult to translate. And she inquired whether it was possible for the interference to be in some way filtered more than it is, to relieve their burden. So I bring that to your attention. Perhaps the technical booth could look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you bring it already to the attention of the technical booth? Not yet. I would have not have opposed if you would have done so, so that during the break we could have. Yes, I can only ask the technicians to see whether they can do anything about it. If it would be useful to have an interval, to have it fixed, then of course we do so. If we can continue and if you could just try to experience whether you can make it any better, that would be even preferable. When I do not hear any explicit request from the technical booth to have a break, we'll just continue and perhaps the speed of our speech might be of some importance as well. Ms. Philpott, you have heard about the technical problems. If there's anything that could be done in Sarajevo, of course, I expect the technicians to be in touch with each other. And let's slowly proceed, then, and see what happens. And may I invite everyone who is facing difficulties they cannot overcome to inform me immediately. Could you then please bring Ms. Pita into the videoroom again. Welcome back, Mrs. Pita. Counsel for the Prosecution will now resume the examination. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Pita, you told us earlier that your daughter was wounded between 10.00 and 11.00 on the -- that is, before noon, on the 13th of December. What was the weather like that morning before your daughter and your husband went off to fetch water?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: The weather was, that night, or rather on the 12th of December, first there was some rain. It was pretty cold. It was late autumn. In the morning, it was dull and overcast and foggy. But it was basically foggy. The visibility was poor after we went for water, and that is when the day broke. It was also dull and overcast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any concerns for your daughter's safety when she went off to collect water with your husband?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Why, yes, always. But that morning, after all that shelling, it was quite quiet and calm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the fact that it was foggy important to you in any way in the decision to let her go with your husband?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: But, of course. But, of course. It was important. It is my child. And believe me, all the time, in the cellar, in the cellar she could barely wait to see some daylight. And all children, many children in that city, fell victim, and they wanted to come out, to come out of the cellar, to come out to see some daylight, some open sky, for all the children, even if it was not easy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Pita, please listen carefully to the questions that I ask you. Could you explain, please, to us the relevance of it being foggy to the decision to let your daughter go with your husband to collect water.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I have already said that. There was major shelling that night. But the morning seemed that a truce had been -- the fire had stopped at around perhaps 5.00 in the morning. We had no water, but we needed water badly. And since there was some rain, we thought that that stream had swollen perhaps a little bit. And because there were so many people who needed water. And she cried and she wanted to go with her father. And I stayed behind to clear the house from what had happened that night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Please, listen to me. Generally before that day, in the weeks and months before that day, in the area where you lived, were people concerned that they could be seen from Serb positions when they moved about outside their houses?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, now please --

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes. My house, where I live, and where I used to live, you can still see it as if the palm of your hand. The entrance into my house faces those lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Pita, if you could please just answer the question that I ask you, I would be very grateful. Now, when people moved about, given that they were concerned, did they move about more freely at night and when the weather made it more difficult for them to be seen from positions held by Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes, at night, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, once again, this was a leading question, because it's not only whether people separated by night, but also with the intention that can be read into it, and I do not think that this question should be admitted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the question has been answered already. I can't imagine that this is a point that may be more in dispute than the last objection raised against a question which would be leading or not leading. Would you please keep that in mind, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us that the fact that it was foggy that morning was relevant to your decision to let your daughter go with your husband to collect water. Could you please explain to us why the fact that it was foggy was relevant to that decision?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness has already answered that question. My learned friend has already asked that question and she answered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness has not in fact responded to that part of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the witness responded to the weather conditions, and it's my recollection that she explained exactly why the rain influenced her decision, but it's not my recollection there was a specific answer to this part of the weather conditions. But if I'm mistaken, then we'll just check it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe, Mr. President, I believe that she was -- that she did speak about that. But I'm speaking from memory. I believe she mentioned visibility. We can check it in the transcript. I was listening to the Serbian, but we can -- I believe that is also somewhere in the English transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the answer was on -- the question was on 72, line 24: "Was the fact that it was foggy important to you in any way in the decision to let her go with your husband?" The answer was, "But of course, but of course, it was important. It's my child, and believe me all the time in the cellar, in the cellar."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. The question was put to the witness, but the answer the witness gave did not really respond to that specific aspect of the question. So the objection is denied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Pita, I will ask you that question again. Could you please explain to us what exactly was the relevance of the fact that it was foggy to your decision to let your daughter go with your husband to collect the water?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: May I say this: I have already said that. I do not know whether that is the specific question. It was foggy. It was dull. It was overcast, as I've said already. But when my daughter went with my husband, and I repeated it several times, and in my statement, the girl was very much attached to her father, and I suppose that she just spent too much time in darkness in the cellar. And like any child, she simply wanted to get out. It was interesting for her to see that water, to see how it's poured, how it's collected, how it's carried and so on. And let me explain it. Whilst they were at that stream, the fog -- the fog had already lifted. The fog was gone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it that by the time your daughter returned to the house, it was no longer foggy, having regard to your last answer. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, whereabouts exactly was your daughter at the moment that she was shot?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, let me explain it to you. As far as I could understand --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Pita, before you explain, could you please listen to me. If you are able to answer my question by simply stating the place, that will be enough. Can you tell us where exactly she was at the moment that she was -- I withdraw that question. I'll ask you another question. Were you actually watching your daughter at the moment she was shot or not? If you can answer that question simply, please do so.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I'll explain it to you. The -- my little girl was taking her shoes off in front of the front door, and I was away from the threshold, about less than half a metre to the left. That is, to the right from the entrance. And I had one foot in the bathroom and the other one in the passage, in the hall. That is how I was standing. And then I heard that shot, as I have already said. I just moved my left foot towards her, towards the front door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that. Now, you have told us that you took her to a clinic for some treatment, and then from the clinic, you took her to Kosevo Hospital. Approximately how far was the clinic from your house?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No, perhaps we didn't understand each other. It was like this: First, we took her to the health centre. That was the health centre before the war, and still is. And we first took her there, but those doctors saw that the bullet had gone through her body, that it was not a minor incident, and then they sent us to the hospital at Kosevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Pita, all right. How far away was the health centre, approximately, from your home?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I always go back to that thing. I will not make it -- I will not specify it, but it could be four, five hundred metres perhaps to the health centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In a moment you will see a video on the screen in front of you. Please watch the video carefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this stage, I would be grateful for Exhibit P3280W to be shown on the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please, could the technicians assist us. I see it's on the screen. Ms. Philpott, could you confirm that it's on the screen as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] We now have it on the screen, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Could you please show me, to the best of your recollection, you were located at the time your daughter Anisa was shot. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Thank you. Can you now please show me by standing on the spot where, to the best of your recollection, Anisa was standing at the time that she was shot. "THE WITNESS: [Interpretation] She was in this position. "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Can you now please point to the spot where, to the best of your recollection, the bullet hole was before the wall was repaired. "THE WITNESS: Here, in the corner. At the corner. While Anisa was on the ground. "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Could you now please point in the direction where, to the best of your recollection, the sound of gunfire came at the time or shortly before the time that Anisa was shot. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Thank you. If you could just hold that position. "Thank you."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Pita, did you recognise yourself in that video?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have to make an observation, and it is the following: It seems to me to be of importance. General, please. The video was necessarily taken before this videolink testimony on the part of the witness. I see that the person interviewing her, Mr. Hogan, used, at least at one point, the expression "when they shot at you." Now, I think that this type of question could be a leading one, because who knows whether this child might have been the victim of a ricocheting bullet. So if she was the victim of ricocheting, then they didn't shoot at her. She was the victim of an accident. And I think that this is an important distinction to be made, and the Defence cannot but object when we come to a cassette like that, a tape like that, because I see the witness with this type of question is being prepared. So the Defence feels that this is not completely honest on the part of the Prosecutor to proceed in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the investigator, Mr. Hogan, spoke in English. I have the benefit of a transcript in English, thanks to the transcript writers in Court. My learned colleague speaks English, and he has put to the Trial Chamber that the investigator used the words "when they shot -- " Excuse me. "When they shot at you." Those words do not appear in the transcript, and I don't recollect having heard them spoken by the investigator, and they are the basis of my friend's complaint. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I think that Mr. Ierace could switch on to the French channel to see what -- hear what I heard. What I just did was to mention the expression, and let me take it up again, in the transcript. Je pense que ce qui... "shot at." C'est cette expression. I think that expression could be contentious, leading, in the sense that if there was a ricochet, there wasn't a shot which would have been targeting the child. So this is a nuance, a shade of meaning, and I found this in page 78, line 13 of the English transcript. And this could lead to some very serious problems, Mr. President, because let me repeat, the tape was filmed before the testimony of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you make an objection against the use of the video since the video would be leading the witness into answering questions. The video has been played by now. We'll consider it and we'll give you a decision. I expect the video to be tendered into evidence. Yes, Mr. Ierace. I don't know whether you understood the objection. The objection was "shooting at." That's the same words you used, and the objection of Mr. Piletta-Zanin was that if it would have been a ricochet, that there would be no situation where someone had been shooting at a person.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The difficulty, Mr. President, is that the words alleged by Mr. Piletta-Zanin are "when they shot at you." The words were not said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have to... Just look at the transcript at how it has been -- Let me just see. Could you guide me, Mr. Ierace, where it is in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "Could you please point in the direction to the best of your recollection..."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I quoted the lines. It was 78:13, and the expression was "she was shot." That's what I said, "she was shot." And that seemed to me to be leading. I don't know what it was translated in in Serbian, because I wasn't able to hear what was said. But I fear it referred to a direct shot, which it might not have been.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It doesn't say direct shot. It doesn't say "shot at." It was "shot." Nothing more, nothing less. We'll give a decision on that. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll ask Your Honours to look also at page 79, line 10, as to what Mr. Piletta-Zanin alleged, but I accept of course that the decision will come later. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Pita, did you recognise yourself in that video?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you carried out the directions of the investigator, did you do so truthfully and to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that the witness be shown in Sarajevo a copy of Photograph Exhibit Number 3266.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Philpott, could you confirm when.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Whilst that's being done, perhaps copies of that exhibit could be distributed in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We see on our screen that it is on the ELMO in Sarajevo now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Pita, can you see that photograph from where you are sitting?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sign that photograph and put on it the date that you signed it?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that on the 25th of September, 2001?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you place a black pen mark on the photograph outlining a tree, a small tree?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that tree there -- I withdraw that. First of all, does the photograph show the view --

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No, this tree was not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell us what can be seen in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: On the photograph, we can see the place. I can't specify. The rock, but it is my opinion that it was the place from which she was hit, and no other place. So on my side, where I am, is the terrace. Between the two houses, across that roof over there. I can't see from this distance very well, but that's where the rock is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You told us --

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Only 5, 6 metres of terrace can be hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us that the photograph shows the terrace between the two houses. Do you mean by that the area from -- please listen to the question -- the area that can be seen from the porch of your house?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes. As if it was on the palm of your hand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think you've already told us that the tree that you outlined in black ink was not there on the date that your daughter was shot. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. The tree was planted actually on the 24th of March, 1994. Because of treatment of my daughter, we all went for treatment. So from the shells and the impact of the shells, this area where the tree is located was a flower bed in fact. As it was a flower bed, there were roses which were damaged by the shelling. After we left to go abroad, in this space, somebody -- one of our relatives planted a cherry tree. It's a young tree. It's a small tree, but you know how long it takes yourself for a tree to grow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Pita, if you are able to answer questions with a simply yes or no, that would be preferred. On the photograph, is it possible to see the place that you called Baba?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I think you can, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you place a mark on the photograph indicating the position of Baba?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I placed an arrow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The position of the arrow seems to be in a white part of the photograph. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No, on the line itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What clothes was your daughter wearing on the morning that she was shot, at that time?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: My little girl was wearing -- and I dressed her myself that morning because it was rather a chilly morning, and she had on the following: She had white tennis shoes with laces, laced up; she had blue dungarees; and she had a dark red jacket, a windjammer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which leg was shot? Which of your daughter's legs was shot, her left leg or her right leg?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: My little girl was wounded in her right leg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, coming back to the time that she was shot, you told us that there was another little girl who arrived back at the house with her. And I think you said that her name was Elma. What was Elma --

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Elma Smajkan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was Elma at the time that Anisa was shot?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Elma had stepped into the hallway and had reached the sitting room, right up to the sitting room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said that she was wearing slippers. Is that correct, that she was wearing slippers?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it that -- withdraw that. Did she take the slippers off before she came inside?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes, she did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see her take the slippers off?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that your daughter had some shoes with laces. Did she have shoes with laces?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've also indicated on the video the position that your daughter was in at the time she was shot, and the position you indicated is that she was crouched over. Is that as you recollect her position at the moment she was shot?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, she was standing up. She went in, crossed the threshold, stepped across the threshold, and I told her to come back to untie her tennis shoes, the laces of her tennis shoes. And as she bent down to untie the laces, that's when she was hit, in that position. Her left leg was in front, and her right leg was a little to the side, so it hit her right in her right leg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that she was taking off the shoes -- withdraw that. You've told us that you turned around to see her immediately after she was shot. When you last saw her immediately before she was shot --

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- was she facing into the house or away from the house or to the side, or what?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No, it was like this. Elma, her friend, had already stepped inside. And the first noise when I was in the bathroom, I heard that she was calling, "Mummy" outside. And she said, "I brought my friend along. Can we play?" And I said -- I told them to take some toys and play around the house where the cellar was, but I saw --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Pita, you told us a few moments ago, "I told her to come back to untie her tennis shoes, the laces of her tennis shoes. As she bent down to untie her laces, that's when she was hit, in that position. Her left leg was to the front and her right leg was to the side so it hit her right in her right leg." My question is simply, at that moment when she was shot, which way was she facing?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: She was facing the door, towards the entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Perhaps before I give the opportunity to the Defence to cross-examine the witness, let me just first give you the decision in relation to the video and the -- whether the question was leading or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. With regard to that issue, what I wanted to point out, and specifically to say, was that the objection includes and essentially includes the fact that this interview was before the telephone transmission [as interpreted], and we are proceeding with the fact, whether it was correct or not, that it was a shot, and it was a wound created by a bullet. As a consequence of that, I think that to proceed in that way represents something which goes along the lines of a leading question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We do not have the statement of the witness. Could you please verify for me whether the statement was of an earlier date, and perhaps could we see the exact date of the video. Because that's the very basis of your objection. The statement was given, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, by Ms. Pita on what date?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the date is the 25th of June, 2001, but I see a telephone mentioned in the transcript. I never said "telephone" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, let's just do one thing after another.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the 25th of June, 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we just see the beginning of the video to see what date the video is, when the video was taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please, I've seen enough. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the basis of your objection is that the video was taken prior to the -- or at least that there was no statement of the witness yet. Does the statement of the witness indicate that her daughter was hit by a bullet?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there is a second statement, and that is dated the 25th, which is posterior to the tape, which is after the tape. But I'm going to check both statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it the case of the Defence that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The statement says, in fact, that she was hit by a bullet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So Mr. Piletta-Zanin, what we see now is that you made an objection based on a line which was not spoken. "Shot at" was not the words spoken as far as I understand. Then you said it was leading the witness. Is it the case of the Defence that the daughter of this witness was not hit by a bullet? I'm not talking about intentionally shot at, but is that the case of the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the problem is that we don't know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just first ask you whether it is the case of the Defence that this girl was not hit by a bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I confer with my lead counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, as we can't know, we cannot say that she was hit by a bullet. Therefore, we're challenging the fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it's the case of the Defence that she was not hit by a bullet. So we'll see and wait what this results in as far as the cross-examination of the witness is concerned and as far as the evidence to be presented by the Defence is concerned. Let me then give you the decision. The Chamber understands that the word "shot" means "hit by a bullet." The Chamber has been informed by now that in a previous statement, previous to this video-taking, that the witness has given a statement including that her daughter was hit by a bullet. Therefore, it's not an acceptable leading, the question put by the investigator to the witness where the daughter was at the time she was shot. So the objection is denied. That's our decision. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Fatima, good day to you.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
