utterances.text: Can you confirm that you gave a statement to the investigators of the Prosecution on the 25th of September, 2001?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes, I can, and I do confirm it. I confirm my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on 25th of June, 2001?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Fatima, you told us that in 1992, you lived in Sarajevo, and the street was Zadrici Street. Can you tell us what local community in the Stari Grad municipality that belongs to?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: It is the Sirokaca local community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that in 1992, April, May, and June, so during that period, that a state of war was proclaimed in Sarajevo and mobilisation was proclaimed as well?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: All I know is that shooting started. Now, what was proclaimed, I don't know. I didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within your local community of Sirokaca, is there a primary school there?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it not true that in that particular school, during the conflict in Sarajevo in 1992, 1993, and 1994, that the army, the soldiers of the BH army, were put up in the primary school building?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. Not in the school, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this period, in 1992, 1993, and 1994, in the part of town you lived in, did you happen to see soldiers of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No. And I said up until when I lived there, the 24th of April, 1994, the whole of my family went for treatment abroad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Fatima, I know that, and that's why I'm asking you about 1992, 1993, and 1994, up until April. That is to say, the period you were there. During that time, did you happen to see BH army soldiers in the part of town you lived in?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your husband, did he have a work obligation to go to his workplace?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your husband a member of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us here today that you had no water. Can you tell us, please, on the territory of the Sirokaca local community, was there a water reservoir anywhere?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No, nowhere. In my area, nowhere in my neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that the barracks called Bistrik, or the barracks at Bistrik, rather, which is 1 kilometre away from where you lived, that that was where the BH army was located? Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I can only remember that before the war, it was the Yugoslav army. As to the BH, I can't say because I don't know and didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how far from your house is the rock which is called Baba, as you say?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Baba is -- I repeat it, I never measured it, and I'm no expert. But with the naked eye, I would say two to three hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what place in relation to your house can you see the Baba rock when you say 200 metres?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I can see it whenever I go into my house or come out of my house. That is what I see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you speak about the Baba rock, are you speaking about a hill which rises above your house where that rock outcrop is, or are you referring to the rock alone?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Both the hill and the rock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you answer what hill, which is the hill that you can see from your house?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Of course I can. It is the hill Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Trebevic a hill or a mountain?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I'd call it a hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long does it take you to reach the hill that you see from your house on foot? I mean in terms of time, how long does it take you to get there?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Well, once upon a time, when I used to go there for outings, it would take me 20 minutes. Now that I am sick, perhaps it would take me an hour or maybe even more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that hill that you can see from your house, and that you tell us is called Trebevic, in relation to your street, is it in the area of Cicin Han or Brajkovac?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: In between. Cicin Han is to the right, and Brajkovac is to the left.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would now like, since the witness has identified the location of the hill which has the Baba rock in relation to the place where she lived, and we would like the witness to see the map of the city of Sarajevo. The Defence has submitted the plan to the officers who were in Sarajevo, and I'd now like to ask that the plan of the city of Sarajevo showing Stari Grad be placed on the ELMO. And in the lower right-hand corner where it says "Stari Grad," will the witness place on the ELMO and mark the place where she lived, in the area of Cicin Han-Brajkovac, and to show us where that hill was in location to the house where she lived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We now see that the map of Sarajevo is on the ELMO in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we focus it, please. Zoom that part where it says "Stari Grad," Sirokaca," and "Cicin Han."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Am I right in understanding it's more to the right?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, I think we're in the right spot now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Fatima --

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I can't see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark the area of Sirokaca, Brajkovac.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I just can't see. And I'm afraid I won't be precise enough. I'm afraid I'll go wrong. It's neither Cicin Han nor Brajkovac. My street is in between. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you then just mark the location of your street, of Zagrici, on the map?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Well, it's that I can't really see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just bring the map down so that we can see.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I can't see. The lettering is just too small. I can't see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you bring the map down, please. Can you just... Can now it be moved upward, please. Can the map be moved upward so that we have on the screen the part of the city that you lived in.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Stari Grad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, will you stop the map there and can we now zoom in, this part of the map.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I can see Cicin Han, but Sirokaca...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you then circle Cicin Han and Brajkovac.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I can't do it. That's not my street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Above Cicin Han and Brajkovac is where you see Sirokaca. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No. No, excuse me. Sirokaca is my neighbourhood community, and Zagrici is between Brajkovac. Zagrici is between these two neighbourhoods. Here it is. Sirokaca. Sorry, I can see it here, but I can't see it there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you circle where you see Sirokaca?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it should be made clear whether the witness is being invited simply to circle the name "Sirokaca," which appears on the map, or Sirokaca as she knows it. I pose that because of the last few answers by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic, I have another problem. On the screen, we can zoom in. The witness indicated several times that she couldn't see it. If you can see it on the screen, this does not automatically mean that you can see it on the map you have to mark as well. Because there, of course, the size of the letters is the original one. So would you please be very precise in --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's just too small, the lettering. I can see it on the screen. I see them, but not on the map itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Mrs. Fatima, you can see Sirokaca on the screen.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes, because it's large letters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see to the left of it where it says Zagrici above Sirokaca?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. I think that Zagrici is somewhere here. I don't know. I really can't find my way around this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in relation to this map, and the place where it says Sirokaca, can you determine the direction of the area which you called Trebevic hill and where the Baba rock is in relation to the neighbourhood of Sirokaca?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I really can see it on the screen, but not on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you underline Sirokaca on the map so that we can see on the screen that you have marked the place called Sirokaca.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I can see Sirokaca on the screen, but on the map the letters are just too small and I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, the witness has now said four or five times that the size of the letters on the map are too small for her to see, and that the only thing -- the only place where she can read any text is when it's enlarged on the screen. So you can't ask her to mark anything on a map which she cannot read. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on the screen you can see -- will you please take a pencil and point at the place where it says Sirokaca.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I can't see here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Could this be it? No, no, no, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see on the screen where it says Sirokaca?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes, I do, on the screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, keep the map that way. Can you, then, place the pencil and show where that is?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Believe me, I cannot circle it because I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's no need for you to circle it. Just place a pencil there. Please, in relation to that place where it says Sirokaca, can you mark -- can you indicate the place which you say is called Brdo Trebevic, in which direction? Just draw a line on the screen to indicate the direction. You don't have to draw anything. Just have to use the pencil to show where is the Trebevic hill.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: It goes from the left to Brajkovac here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But your pencil there, and show us where Trebevic is.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I think that the hill is like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to Brajkovac where?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Brajkovac, I think is to the left. I don't know. I really can't focus here. I can't see on the map because I don't see it. I see the letters on the screen very well. But I cannot point on the screen and look at the map, and the map is just -- the lettering is too small, and I can't see anything and I therefore cannot point there. On the screen, perhaps, yes. Would you please move to your next question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, how far is the Trebevic hill from your street, from the place where you live?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Well, once again, I don't know where to. The rock? I told you how long it takes you. And where Trebevic is, you know where Trebevic is, above the road towards Jahorina. Perhaps you don't know it but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Baba rock within -- is it a part of Trebevic hill?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. That is one and the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it at the foot of that hill or somewhere above it?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I can't be precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you look from your terrace, you said that you can see it as if in the palm of your hand. Can you see both the hill and the rock, or the rock only?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: All I can see is the rock, and above the rock is a pylon, is a high-voltage pylon that is there on that rock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how high is that rock?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Believe me, I didn't measure it. I know it's high, but how, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the direction in which you are looking from your house towards the Baba rock, is there a wooded part of that hill?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Excuse me, could you repeat the question? Do you mean the rock itself, or between my terrace and the rock?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between your terrace to the rock.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Why, yes, there are some fruit trees, and there is nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But is there any forest, any woods?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes. And above the rock --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And above the rock, any woods there?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us in relation to the rock and the hill that you see from your house, how far are the front lines, in relation to your house, looking in that direction?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I already said that the distance was about 200 to 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of that distance of two to three hundred metres, which army was there?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, where were the front lines of the BH army, looking in that direction, and how far were they from your house?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No, I did not see that, and I don't know. And what I didn't see, I cannot tell you about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I will now show you a part of your statement that you gave to the investigators of the OTP on the 25th of June, 2001, page 3, paragraph 3 in your statement on page 3. In English, that would be that Document Number 0208-1039. In the English version, that is paragraph 3. And I will read to you only one line from your statement: "The front lines were toward the top of the hill. That was where the defenders were." When you said that -- did you say this?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: The defenders. I don't remember saying that. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you are telling us, aren't you, that a part of the statement in your statement, which is on the page which I showed to you, where you say the front lines were toward the top of the hill, that is where the defenders were, are you saying that you did not state that?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Well, it could be an error, a mistake. But believe me when I say that it was the troops of Republika Srpska who were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, in that direction, when you said that the defenders were in that direction, did you mean the army of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Sorry, I said the army of Republika Srpska, but I just don't remember saying "defenders." And please, don't repeat the same question over and over again. I've already answered that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Fatima, can you tell us if from your house when you come out into the street, whether from that direction you can also see the Baba rock?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No. Only from the terrace, from in front of the door. The terrace is about 4 or 5 metres long, and it could be hit only from there. And once again, sorry, there is this child, the child, and the wound, and my door, and the Baba rock, and there you are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you took your daughter first to the health centre, is it? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, you took her to the Kosevo Hospital?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that for ten days, you had to take her there to have her wound dressed?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do the hospital records -- does the hospital record show that your daughter was admitted into the hospital and were you given some medical documentation?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes, the letter of discharge says clearly "wounded by a sniper bullet." I stated that I had lost all this hospital documentation when I was abroad, and you can go and look at their records. It is there when we took the child and all that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you answer on the basis of what do you claim that your daughter had been hit by a bullet?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I can confirm first because I was on the spot; secondly, because that bullet was so hot; thirdly, the paper, the documents, when we carried her to the hospital, that is what the doctors put down. That is what they wrote down, what she had been wounded by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You tell us that the bullet was hot. So you tell us that you had seen that bullet?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes. I saw it, and I kept it until recently. And I'm really sorry that I could not show it today to this Honourable Court. I lost it. And even if I found it -- and that is also possible. If I find it, I will show it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you gave your statement to the OTP investigators, did you give your statement in the Serbian language or in the English language?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I gave my statement in my mother tongue, which is Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are saying that you gave the statement in your mother tongue, and it was then translated into English?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that, was it read to you? Was the statement read out to you, the statement which was translated into English and which you signed in English?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you, with your signature, confirm that what had been read to you from the statement was what you had said to the OTP investigators?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I stand by my statement, and it's all as it is, 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are confirming that you stated that the front lines were to the top of the hill, and that the defenders were there?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No. The army of Republika Srpska, not on the hill but on the rock, up the hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I merely read to you what you claim you stated.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes, madam. Please ask me whatever you like. I'm here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that you stated - and I'll quote it to you once again - I'll quote to you a part of your statement that you confirmed today that you stand by it and all that the statement says is true and reflected faithfully what you had said. I'll read it once again. Is it true when you say in your statement, "The front lines were towards the top of the hill. That was where the defenders were." Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No, no, I confirm my statement. But I do not recall that, and it could be a misunderstanding. That is not what I said, and I do not think that that was how it was. I will always stand by it, that those were the lines of the army of Republika Srpska. And you can check it with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where were the front lines where the members of the army of BH were and which they held?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Please, I cannot confirm it for you because I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst the conflict went on and you lived in your house, did you ever go in the direction of Baba rock?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the soldiers of the army of Republika Srpska there?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No. And I never looked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the basis of what do you claim that it was the positions of the army of Republika Srpska on the Baba rock?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Well, I'll explain it to you. I have already said, and repeatedly so, that in my cellar, there was no toilet so that we had to go upstairs. And as we went there -- and in my cellar, there were at times 20, 30 people from all over the neighbourhood, children and adults. So don't you think that we need toilets?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: And will you please wait until I finish. So as we went upstairs, we could see fire because it was all dark. And we could see some -- the fire, and whenever I went upstairs, I could see the fire coming from that direction, from Baba rock --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just interrupt you. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you are discussing in a loud voice, perhaps not aware that you're having headphones. If there's any need to have any discussion with lead counsel, please ask to be permitted to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] My apologies to this, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic, may I ask you another question first. Ms. Pilipovic, we are approximately at the time at which we intended to finish for today. Could you tell us how much time you'd still need so that we can see whether we can conclude the examination of this witness or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think I'll need another 10 to 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you make it 10 minutes, Ms. Pilipovic, then I think we could conclude. Some of the Judges have other obligations this afternoon. Please proceed, and try to make it as effective and efficient as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The Defence is always faced with that problem in the course of its cross-examination, that it has to be efficacious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I remind you Ms. Pilipovic that I noticed several times the Prosecution, when the witness was giving very long answers, tried to interfere and make it effective. So I think you're facing similar problems. In the second half of the trial, you'll be the one who will be examining in chief your witnesses and it will be the Prosecution who has to cross-examine the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, that is certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us whether you saw soldiers belonging to the army of Republika Srpska at Mount Baba -- sorry, Rock Baba?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that on the night between the 12th and 13th, that there was shelling.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes. And the whole night at that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, in the area your house is located in, whether any shells fell in that area?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Around my house, and around all the houses, and today, too, when a lot has been reconstructed and built up --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I asked you whether any shells fell around your house, and if so, how many. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many shells fell during that night on your house or by your house?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Six fell on my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if I tell you that your husband, on page 4011, was interviewed on the 19th of February, 2002, said that in June, five or six mines fell around your house, can you tell us which of the two is correct?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Please, the war began on the 6th of April, 1992. From that time on, the shelling was not in April, one April and another April. Shelling was throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us who waged the war in Sarajevo and in your part of town? Who were the warring sides? Who went to war?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I think the war was led by the former Yugoslav People's Army and the Serb army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody wage a war against those two armies?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I don't know that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Fatima, can you answer the following: Do you know whether on the 13th and on the 12th of February -- December, I mean December, in the Sarajevo city area, were there battles for the hill of Zuc and also was there fighting for the Otes area? Was there fighting between the two armies over those few days?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I don't know. I saw to my children. I was busy thinking what we would eat, how we could get some water. I live in Stari Grad. I don't know where Zuc is. I don't know where all those other places are. I apologise, but I just don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission, the Defence would like to proffer a document which is in English. And my colleague would quote a passage or, rather, two lines from document entitled "Annex 6 for the 13th of December, 1992." It is a situation report on the front on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think the usual procedure is that we are provided with a copy of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I expected Mr. Piletta-Zanin will give to the usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may the document be given a number straight away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's D73, is it not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll ask the registry. What was the number of the map which was shown to the witness which was not prenumbered by you, and do you want to tender that into evidence since there were no markings made on the map finally? I think it's not of great use, but I leave it up to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then the map will not be tendered into evidence. And the next number, Madam Registrar, would then be?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D74. So no number for the map. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Having settled the matter, Mr. President, may I continue with the reading of the passage?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's first see that it's distributed. Yes, please read it slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. After a date, which is the 13th of December, 1992, and in brackets, it says, [In English] "Sunday, activity combat and shelling activity, after BiH forces reportedly gained control of Zuc hill, Serb artillery began pounding the area. Source is Reuters. Targets hit Zuc hill. Source is Reuters." End of quotation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you confirm that in the part of town and relative to where you live, that Zuc hill is to be located?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Not where I live, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us with respect to your area where Zuc hill is?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know that in the period between the 12th and 13th of December, that fighting took place to gain control of Zuc hill?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: I don't know. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on the photograph, you indicated to us the direction -- a direction. Can you tell us whether the direction, where it says "Baba," whether you actually indicated the place where the rock is located? Where it says "Baba" and your arrow, is that where the rock is?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission, could the witness just be shown the photograph for a brief moment because I have a question to ask her. May it be placed on the ELMO, please. It is Document 3266. All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you now show us on the photograph the arrow and the word "Baba." Can you show us the direction that the hill or rock called Baba is located? Can you elongate the arrow to show us the direction of Baba rock.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: It's here somewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you draw a circle around the spot, please. A circle, please, and put in the number 1. Put 1 in the circle.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And for the transcript, this circle denotes the area in which Baba rock or Baba hill is located. Your Honour, the Defence has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic. Let me first clarify that we have one exhibit tendered here in The Hague, which is number P3266. We have a similar -- I should talk about a document and not about an exhibit yet. We also have a document which is in Sarajevo and which is marked as well. So we have two marked documents, but markings... Although usually we use one exhibit number, I would suggest that under these circumstances, the photograph in Sarajevo gets a D number, because it's marked in Sarajevo. Or would we do it differently?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, could I suggest, there are one or two questions I'd seek to ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps we should do that first, and only then talk about the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And if time is precious, perhaps we could do it tomorrow morning. Mr. President, one of the questions, I confess, may go beyond re-examination. It's one question. I'd seek your leave to ask that on the presumption it goes go beyond re-examination. Perhaps I'll ask the question, and my friend could object if she wishes. If it does go beyond re-examination, of course, I'll be happy to ask further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. Pita, a question will be put to you now by Mr. Ierace, but would you wait for a second to answer that question because there might be an objection against it. We'll see. Mr. Ierace, please proceed. Re-examined by Mr. Ierace:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Pita, you said that you saw the bullet that wounded your daughter and that it was hot. Do you know the calibre of the bullet?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. No, I don't. I don't understand those things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The answer was given immediately. Given the answer --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: One further question which is squarely within re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that as you made your way to the toilet from the basement at nighttime, you would see sometimes fire coming from Baba rock. Could you tell us more about the fire that you saw. Was it single shots, repeated shots as in a machine-gun, tracer bullets, or what?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA PITA
utterances.text: Mostly they were shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Ierace. Mrs. Pita, you've answered all the questions of the parties. There were so many questions that the Judges don't have any additional questions to put to you. Thank you very much for coming and for giving your testimony. This concludes --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Philpott, tomorrow morning, the first thing we'll do in the morning is to deal with the documents. Especially would you keep in your custody the marked photograph P3266. We'll give a decision on that tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] Yes, Your Honour. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your assistance. May I also thank the parties for their flexibility to stay until a quarter to 3.00. May I also thank the interpreters for continuing their job beyond the usual times, and the same, of course, as well for the technical assistants. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I'd like to discuss whatever it is tomorrow unless it is about our Court schedule or time schedule.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite. Just to say that we will also produce two exhibits with respect to this witness's statement, if we may be permitted to do so tomorrow, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I referred already to one, that would be the photograph marked, and the other one would be the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is why I wanted to broach this matter now. The witness said that she had not said this or that when faced with her statement. That is why we would like to produce her statements. But we haven't copied them. We haven't got copies of her statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As far as I understood, you read literally what the witness said. So as such, there's no need for the Chamber -- since there has been no objection from the Prosecution, I take it that you literally quoted her and that she denied having said that during her testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then everything is clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, then. And we'll adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, same courtroom -- same courtroom is not quite sure. Would you please find out -- it will be the same courtroom, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be the same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
